description.p: Neatpad is a plain text editor that opens files of any size at once, from a short note to a log or disk image several gigabytes long. It reads only what it shows, so scrolling and editing stay quick however large the file is.

ul.li: Unsaved changes are kept as you type, and come back after a crash or when the window is closed
UTF-8, UTF-16, UTF-32 and Latin-1, with Windows, Unix and Mac line endings, each kept as the file has them
Find and replace, with every match highlighted, or only the matching lines shown
Follow File shows what another program adds to a log as it writes it
Line numbers, changed lines marked in the margin, and control characters shown
Light and dark styles, and colour palettes of your own

screenshot.caption: Filter a large log down to the lines that matter

ul.li: Turning Filter on or off keeps the caret on its line, rather than jumping to the start of the file
Following a file with Filter on shows new matching lines as they're written
Faster search when not matching case

description.p: The first release for Linux: Neatpad as a GNOME app, alongside the Windows version.

ul.li: Open huge files and logs at once, follow them as they grow, and filter them to the lines that matter
Unsaved changes are kept as you type, and come back when you open the file again
Save in another encoding or with other line endings
Light and dark styles, your accent colour, and colour palettes
